attributes.name: bgtransparent
attributes.digest: Toggles background transparency
attributes.description: Toggles background transparency. The messagesets the background of theobject to transparent. When set to 1, the background of the object remains transparent until you clear it using themessage. When the attribute value is set to 0 (the default) the background is initially white, consistent with earlier versions of Max.

attributes.name: border
attributes.digest: Toggles the drawing of a border around theobject's window, which is on by default. A message ofturns this feature off.
attributes.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, toggles the drawing of a border around theobject's window, which is on by default. A message ofturns this feature off.

The first number is the number of pixels to the right of that corner, and the second number is the number of pixels down from that corner.turns off this feature, which is off by default.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: You can draw freehand inwith the mouse (provided this feature has not been turned off with a local 0 message). The mouse will draw with the current pen and color characteristics, and the mouse location will be sent out the outlet.

messages.name: anything
messages.digest: refers to the backwards-compatible capitalized messages.
messages.description: refers to the backwards-compatible capitalized messages.

messages.name: ascii
messages.description: The word, followed by a number between 0 and 255, writes the character corresponding to that ASCII value at the current pen position, then moves the pen position to the right of that character. Numbers that exceed the 0-255 range are restricted to that range with a modulus operation.

messages.name: backsprite
messages.digest: Set a named sprite's drawing order so that it is drawn first/displayed last
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, sets the named sprite's drawing order so that it is drawn first (and displayed last). This command can be used to alter the order in which sprites are drawn. (Normally, sprites are drawn in the order they are recorded.)

messages.name: clearpicts
messages.digest: Delete all of anobject's named pictures.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, deletes all of anobject's named pictures from memory so that they can no longer be drawn. To remove the images from theobject's display, the command should be followed by amessage.

messages.name: clearsprites
messages.description: Deletes all of anobject's named sprites.

messages.name: closesprite
messages.digest: Stop sprite command collection and associate the defined region with a name
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol argument that names the sprite, turns off sprite command collection and associates the defined region with the symbol. After themessage, drawing commands function normally again.

messages.name: color
messages.digest: Specify a Max color palette selection for drawing graphics
messages.description: Max color palette selections are specified by a number in the range 0 - 255. Values exceeding 255 are range-restricted using a modulus operation.

messages.name: deletepict
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, deletes the named the picture from memory so that it can no longer be drawn. To remove the image from theobject's display, the command should be followed by amessage.

messages.name: deletesprite
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, deletes the named sprite.

messages.name: drawpict
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, draws the named picture. Optionally there may follow four numbers specifying a destination rectangle in which the picture is scaled and drawn, and source rectangle that specifies the area of the picture to use in the operation. These rectangles are specified as left, top, width, and height values in pixels. The destination rectangle is relative to the top left corner of thedisplay area. The source rectangle is relative to the top, left corner of the picture. If not present, these rectangles are both set to be the same size as the picture.

messages.name: drawsprite
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, draws the named sprite. Optionally this may be followed by a pair of numbers that specify a horizontal and vertical offset for drawing the sprite.

messages.name: font
messages.digest: Specify a font ID and a font size for text drawing
messages.description: Themessage specifies a font ID using the font number mapping that Max 6 uses generally and a font size to select a font used when drawing text in response to aormessage.

messages.name: framearc
messages.description: Same asexcept that only the unfilled outline of the arc is drawn.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, start-angle:degrees, degrees-arc:degrees, red:int?, green:int?, blue:int?

messages.name: frameoval
messages.description: Same asexcept that only the unfilled outline of the oval is drawn.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, red:int?, green:int?, blue:int?

messages.name: framepoly
messages.description: Same asexcept that only the unfilled outline of the polygon is drawn.

messages.name: framerect
messages.description: Same asexcept that only the unfilled outline of the rectangle is drawn.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, red:int?, green:int?, blue:int?

messages.name: frameroundrect
messages.description: Same asexcept that only the unfilled outline of the rounded rectangle is drawn.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, horizontal-roundness:int, vertical-roundness:int, red:int?, green:int?, blue:int?

messages.name: frontsprite
messages.digest: Set a named sprite's drawing order so that it is drawn last/displayed first
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, sets the named sprite's drawing order so that it is drawn last (and displayed first). This command can be used to alter the order in which sprites are drawn. (Normally, sprites are drawn in the order they are recorded.)

messages.name: getpenloc
messages.description: The wordoutputs a message consisting of the wordfollowed by two numbers, out theobject's right outlet. The numbers represent local coordinates relative to the top-left corner of thedisplay area. The first number is the number of pixels to the right of that corner, and the second number is the number of pixels down from that corner.

messages.name: getpixel
messages.description: The word, followed by two integers specifying an offset from the top left corner of theobject's display, sends a message consisting of the wordfollowed by three numbers that specify the color of the pixel in RGB format and two additional numbers that specify the pixel offset.

messages.name: getsize
messages.digest: Output the largest size of thecanvas (patching / presentation).
messages.description: Ouputs a message from the right outlet consisting of the wordand two numbers which report the width and height in pixels of thedisplay area.

messages.name: hidesprite
messages.digest: Disable the drawing of a named sprite

messages.name: line
messages.digest: Draw a line and move the pen position
messages.description: The word, followed by two int arguments for horizontal and vertical offset, in pixels, relative to the current pen position, draws a line from the current pen position to a point determined by the specified offset, and that point becomes the new pen position. Positive arguments draw the line to the right or down; negative arguments draw up or to the left.

messages.name: linesegment
messages.description: The word, followed by four int arguments that specify the endpoints of a line segment, draw a line. The numbers represent the horizontal and vertical offset of the beginning endpoint, and the horizontal and vertical offset of the finishing endpoint, in pixels, relative to the top left corner of thedisplay area. A color may optionally be specified using a single number that selects a color from Max's color palette (similar to themessage), or by using three additional numbers that describe an RGB value (similar to themessage).
messages.argPattern: x start:int, y start:int, x end:int, y end:int

messages.name: lineto
messages.description: The word, followed by two int arguments for horizontal and vertical ending point, draws a line from the current pen position to the position specified by the arguments.

messages.name: move
messages.description: Moves the pen position a certain number of pixels down from, and to the right of, its current position. The wordmust be followed by two int arguments for horizontal and vertical offset, in pixels, relative to the current pen position. Negative arguments may be used to move the pen position up or to the left.

messages.name: moveto
messages.description: Sets the pen position at which the next graphic instruction will be drawn. Themessage must include two int arguments for horizontal and vertical offset, in pixels, relative to the upper left corner of thedisplay area.

messages.name: oprgb
messages.description: The word, followed by three numbers between 0 and 255, specify an RGB value used as the opcolor for penmodes that support it.If the penmode is set to 32, the alpha channel value is derived by averaging the three RGB values and mapping the average to the range 0. - 1.0 (e.g., an oprgb value of 128 128 128 would have an alpha value of .5 when the penmode is set to 32).

messages.name: paintarc
messages.description: The word, followed by six int arguments that specify the left, top, right, and bottom extremities of an oval across which the arc will be drawn, the start angle (0 is the top) and degrees of arc, paints an arc.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, start-angle:degrees, degrees-arc:degrees, red:int?, green:int?, blue:int?

messages.name: paintoval
messages.description: The word, followed by four int arguments specifying the left, top, right, and bottom extremities of an oval, paints an oval. These extremities are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of thedisplay area. A color may optionally be specified using a single number that selects a color from Max's color palette (similar to themessage), or by using three additional numbers that describe an RGB value (similar to themessage).
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, red:int?, green:int?, blue:int?

messages.name: paintpoly
messages.description: The wordmay be followed by as many as 254 int arguments that would specify a series of x/y pairs that define a polygon to be painted in. These x/y pairs are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of thedisplay area.

messages.name: paintrect
messages.description: Left, top, right and bottom positions for the rectangle are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of thedisplay area when painting a filled rectangle. A color may optionally be specified using a single number that selects a color from Max's color palette (similar to themessage), or by using three additional numbers that describe an RGB value (similar to themessage).
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, red:int?, green:int?, blue:int?

messages.name: paintroundrect
messages.description: The word, followed by six int arguments specifying the left, top, right, and bottom positions of a rectangle and the amount of horizontal and vertical roundness in pixels, paints a rounded rectangle. The edge positions are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of thedisplay area. A color may optionally be specified using a single number that selects a color from Max's color palette (similar to themessage), or by using three additional numbers that describe an RGB value (similar to themessage).
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, horizontal-roundness:int, vertical-roundness:int, red:int?, green:int?, blue:int?

messages.name: penmode
messages.description: The word, followed by a number in the range 0-7, sets the transfer mode for subsequent drawing operations. The following are transfer mode constants;Copy 0Or 1Xor 2Bic 3NotCopy 4NotOr 5NotXor 6NotBic 7

messages.name: pensize
messages.description: The word, followed by two equal int arguments specifying horizontal and vertical thickness in pixels (e.g., 4 4), sets the current pensize. The horizontal and vertical thicknesses must be equal.

messages.name: readpict
messages.digest: Read a picture file from disk into RAM
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a symbol which specifies a filename, looks for a graphic file (afile openable on Windows using the QuickTime Picture Viewer for Windows) with that name in Max's file search path, and reads the picture file from disk into RAM. This named picture can then be drawn inwith theandmessages. In response to themessage, the object sends a message out the right outlet of theobject consisting of the wordfollowed by a symbol which specifies the name of the picture file and two numbers which specify the file's width and height. If the read is unsuccessful, the error messagewill be sent out the right outlet.

messages.name: recordsprite
messages.digest: Record drawing commands to be stored in a named sprite
messages.description: Initiates the recording of drawing commands which will be stored in a named sprite. While recording, drawing commands will have no effect on the contents of theobject's window.

messages.name: reset
messages.digest: Erase the contents of thedisplay and reset the pen state
messages.description: Themessage erases the current display and resets the colors, pen, and pen position to their default states. It is equivalent to the message

messages.name: scrollrect
messages.digest: Define a rectangle and move its contents
messages.description: The word, followed by six int arguments that specify the left, top, right, and bottom positions of a rectangle to be scrolled and the number of pixels to scroll in the x and y direction, scrolls a rectangle within theobject's display area.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, x-offset:int, y-offset:int

messages.name: setpixel
messages.digest: Change the color of a pixel
messages.description: The word, followed by two numbers which specify a location in local coordinates relative to the top-left corner of the lcd display area and a list of three integers in the range 0-255 which specify a color in RGB format, will set the pixel at the designated location to the selected color.
messages.argPattern: x coordinate:int, y coordinate:int, red:int?, green:int?, blue:int?

messages.name: size
messages.description: The word, followed by two integers, changes theobject window size. The Maximum size is 8192 x 8192.

messages.name: textface
messages.digest: The wordSet a text style for text rendering
messages.description: The word, followed by one or more names specifying text style(s), sets the font style(s) to be used when rendering text. Text style names are,, and.

messages.name: tilepict
messages.digest: Fill a rectangle by tiling a picture
messages.description: The word, followed by a picture name argument, fills a rectangle by tiling a picture. Optionally there may follow, four numbers that specify a destination rectangle in which the picture is tiled and four numbers that specify a source rectangle that specifies the area of the picture to use in the operation. These rectangles are specified as left, top, width, and height values in pixels. The destination rectangle is relative to the top left corner of thedisplay area. The source rectangle is relative to the top, left corner of the picture. If not present, the destination rectangle is set to the same size of, and the source rectangle is set to be the same size as the picture.

messages.name: write
messages.digest: Write a symbol and move the pen position
messages.description: The word, followed by any symbol, writes that symbol beginning at the current pen position, and moves the pen position to the end of the text.

messages.name: writepict
messages.digest: Save the display area as a PNG file
messages.description: The word, followed by an optional filename argument, writes the current contents of thedisplay area to a PNG file.
